==English==

===Etymology===
From {{der|en|enm|awaiten}}, from {{der|en|fro-nor|awaitier||to lie in wait for, watch, observe}}, originally especially with a hostile sense; itself from {{m|fro|a-||to}} + {{m|fro|waitier||to watch}}.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref> More at {{cog|en|wait}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əˈweɪt/|a=UK}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-await.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪt|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|formal}} To [[wait for]].
#: {{ux|en|I '''await''' your reply to my letter.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=2|passage=I had occasion […] to make a somewhat long business trip to Chicago, and on my return […] I found Farrar '''awaiting''' me in the railway station. He smiled his wonted fraction by way of greeting, […], and finally leading me to his buggy, turned and drove out of town.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[expect]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[in store]] for; to be [[ready]] or [[in waiting]] for.
#: {{ux|en|Glorious rewards '''await''' the good in heaven; eternal suffering '''awaits''' mortal sinners in hell.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To [[serve]] or [[attend]]; to [[wait on]], [[wait upon]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[watch]], [[observe]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To wait; to stay in waiting.
#: {{ux|en|These are exotic lands where great adventures '''await'''.}}

====Usage notes====
* As '''await''' means ''to wait for'', it is not followed by "for". ''*I am awaiting for your reply'' is therefore incorrect.

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|wait for}} {{l|en|wait for}}, {{l|en|anticipate}}, {{l|en|listen}} (of a sound); See also [[Thesaurus:wait for]]
* {{sense|serve or attend}} {{l|en|attend to}}, {{l|en|service}}; See also [[Thesaurus:serve]]

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|awaitable|awaiter|awaitment|reawait}}
